content: Oregon State University (OSU) is a coeducational public research university located in Corvallis, Oregon, United States. It offers undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral degrees, along with extensive research opportunities. The university provides over 200 academic degree programs, and several of its programs, such as nuclear engineering, ecology, forestry, public health, biochemistry, zoology, oceanography, food science, and pharmacy, are nationally recognized as top-tier. In recent years, OSU's liberal arts programs have also expanded significantly, with the College of Liberal Arts becoming one of the largest programs on campus. Since its founding, more than 200,000 individuals have attended OSU. Oregon State is one of 73 land-grant universities worldwide and is also designated as a sea-grant, space-grant, and sun-grant institution. This makes it one of only two universities globally to hold all four designations, with Cornell University being the other. OSU is the only public university to achieve this distinction. The university receives more annual research funding than all other public higher education institutions in Oregon combined. OSU offers more majors, minors, and special programs than any other university or college in Oregon. A 2007 study ranked OSU higher in academic merit than any other institution in the state, placing it among the top 70 universities in the United States and the top 150 in the world. OSU is widely regarded as the nation's leading forestry school, with its College of Forestry ranked first in North America for professional publications, citations, and academic reputation. Research is a cornerstone of OSU's operations, with most activities centered on the Corvallis campus. However, the university also conducts research at various locations across the state and internationally. Notable facilities include the Seafood Laboratory in Astoria, the Food Innovation Laboratory in Portland, and the Hatfield Marine Science Center in Newport. OSU operates two oceanographic research vessels and manages extensive forest land, including the McDonald-Dunn Research Forest. The university is classified as a Comprehensive Doctoral with Medical/Veterinary institution and is the only university in Oregon with Very High Research Activity as per the Carnegie Classification. OSU was one of the original participants in the National Sea Grant College Program and later became a member of the federal Space Grant program in 1991. In 2003, it was designated a federal Sun Grant institution, making it one of only two universities with all four grant designations. The university's Valley Library underwent a $40 million renovation in 1999 and was named Library of the Year by the Library Journal, the first academic library to receive this honor. OSU's Wave Research Laboratory is a leading facility for tsunami research and coastal engineering. The university's history dates back to 1856 with the establishment of Corvallis Academy, which later became Corvallis College. In 1868, it was designated as Oregon's Agricultural College under the Morrill Act, becoming a land-grant institution. Over the years, the institution underwent several name changes, finally becoming Oregon State University in 1961. The campus, located in the fertile Willamette Valley, is known for its tree-lined streets and classical architecture, adhering to the original master plan developed in 1909. OSU recently opened a branch campus in Bend, known as OSU-Cascades, to serve students in central Oregon. The university is organized into 12 colleges and two schools, each led by a dean responsible for faculty, staff, students, and academic programs. Notable colleges include the College of Agricultural Sciences, College of Engineering, College of Veterinary Medicine, and College of Liberal Arts. OSU boasts a distinguished list of alumni, including two-time Nobel Prize winner Linus Pauling, NASA astronauts, Pulitzer Prize winners, and prominent entrepreneurs. The university is also committed to fostering entrepreneurship, with Weatherford Hall dedicated to the Austin Entrepreneurship Program, which supports student business ventures. Student life at OSU is vibrant, with over 300 active student organizations and proximity to numerous outdoor recreational opportunities, including forests, rivers, and the Cascade Range. The majority of older students live off-campus, but on-campus housing is available, primarily for freshmen. The campus features 12 residence halls and the LaSells Stewart Center, a hub for conferences and performing arts. Athletics play a significant role at OSU, with the beaver as its mascot since 1910. The university is a member of the Pacific Coast Conference and has a storied rivalry with the University of Oregon, highlighted by the annual Civil War football game. OSU's baseball team has won two NCAA Division I championships, and its marching band, established in 1890, is the oldest in the Pac-10. OSU is committed to diversity, with a student body that includes in-state, out-of-state, and international students. The university supports diversity through various organizations, cultural centers, and the Office of Community and Diversity. Cultural centers include those dedicated to Native American, African American, and Hispanic communities.
